project: NLRC Street Runner — World 3: Desert Canyon
updated: round 5 — critic gaps 1/3/5 addressed (wall framing reverted, sun raised for shadows, glossy rails). Still short of the reference: sky remains washed out.

gaps.title: BIGGEST REMAINING GAP — the sky is still a flat pale field and dominates the frame
items: The sky gradient stops are spread over the full 0..1 hemisphere, but the camera only ever samples roughly -5deg to +35deg of elevation. Almost the entire visible sky therefore samples the two lightest stops (skyLow/skyHorizon) and reads as one cream wash. FIX: remap `t` in sky.js from dir.y through a curve that expands the 0..0.35 band across the whole ramp, so the peach->violet->blue transition actually happens inside the visible frame.

The sun disc is not visible anywhere in frame. SUN_DIR is (0.34, 0.30, 1.0) which is ~16deg elevation and ~19deg to the right of forward - that should be on screen with a 62deg FOV. Either the disc smoothstep threshold (0.018-0.030 rad) is too tight to survive the 2-level bloom downsample, or the horizon haze term (0.50 mix at low elevation) is washing it out. Needs isolating by temporarily disabling the haze mix.
Cloud decks are invisible: `cover` is multiplied by smoothstep(0.015,0.26,dir.y), so clouds only exist above ~15deg elevation, which is the thin strip at the very top of frame. Lower that threshold.

Canyon walls now frame the shot correctly (gap #1 fixed) but still read as pale flat slabs because fog far=430 desaturates them. The strata texture work is done and good - it is being erased by fog. Either push fog far to ~700 or darken the fog colour further.

Shadows: sun raised to 16deg and frustum tightened to 44x44m, but shadows are still not confirmed visible in a capture. Needs a gameplay-state capture (the menu overlay covers the ground where shadows would fall).

STILL UNVERIFIED: tunnel, trestle bridge, sand storm and mesa zones, and a head-on train, are all implemented but have never been captured. tools/shoot.py has scripted states for all of them; it needs a run with a longer per-shot timeout (SwiftShader renders at <1fps in this sandbox, so the frame-count waits time out).

streams.name: Render Pipeline Correctness
streams.goal: Frame is lit, colour-managed and free of clipping/culling bugs before any art judgement is made.

rounds.note: Captured first real frame: fully black sky, everything ~2 stops dark.
Diagnosed sky as clip-plane culling (r=4000 sphere vs far=900). Rewrote as fullscreen ray-reconstruction quad.
Diagnosed darkness as missing linear→sRGB encode in the custom composite shader. Fixed. Frame is now correctly exposed.

streams.name: Performance & Boot
streams.goal: Sub-2s boot, bounded texture/geometry/material counts, adaptive quality.

rounds.note: Boot was 92s — per-pixel JS noise in texture generation.
Rewrote noise to low-res lattice + native upscale. Boot 92s → 1.5s.
Seed quantisation: 3000+ textures → 82 unique, 533ms total.
Shared geometry cache: 3032 geometries → 344, hit rate 0.9+.

next: level-ready is still 19s — chunk generation itself now dominates, needs profiling

streams.goal: Peach→violet→blue ramp, low readable sun, drifting cloud decks, crepuscular rays, horizon haze.

rounds.note: Shader dome: 5-stop gradient, sun disc + 3 scatter lobes, 3 fbm cloud decks.
Rewritten as fullscreen ray-reconstruction quad to escape clip culling.
Darkened the horizon/low stops. Still reads as a flat pale field — CRITIC REJECTS.

CRITIC REJECTS again. Root cause now identified precisely: gradient stops are spread over the full hemisphere while the camera only samples -5..+35deg, so the visible sky is entirely the two lightest stops. Needs an elevation remap, not new colours.

next: remap dir.y so the ramp happens inside the visible 0-35deg band
lower the cloud elevation threshold
isolate why the sun disc is invisible
